title: GitHub - norifm/nori: blazingly fast multi-platform navidrome client
excerpt: blazingly fast multi-platform navidrome client. Contribute to norifm/nori development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
A music player for your own Navidrome or Subsonic server, on Android, desktop, the terminal and the iPod touch.

Still in development. nori changes quickly: its screens and settings will change between versions, and it will soon get its own design language. Bugs and ideas are welcome in Issues.

   

  • Sleeps between bursts. Music is decoded ahead and the CPU sleeps in between; nothing ticks with the screen off.
  • Sounds right. Gapless albums, AutoMix transitions on the beat, an equalizer with AutoEQ curves, a sound for each output.
  • Finds the words. Your server's lyrics first, then lyrics services online, scored, word by word where they have it.
  • One core, every screen. One Rust core plays, queues and decides; each app only draws.
  • Yours. No nori account or analytics; connect your own server account, and downloads play offline.

Install

  • Android: the APK from the latest release, or see norifm.com.
  • Desktop and terminal: Linux and macOS packages for ARM64 and x86-64 are in the latest release. Use the download picker or follow the installation guide.
  • iPod touch (6th generation, iOS 12, jailbroken): the .ipa from the latest release, and the iPod guide.

Links

Website · Docs · Changelog · Contributing

Build

cargo test -j4 --workspace                            # Rust tests, including doctests
cargo run --release -p nori-desktop                   # the desktop client
cargo run --release -p nori-cli                       # the terminal client
tools/check.sh android -PrustTargets=arm64-v8a         # a debug Android APK

Android builds need the Android SDK, NDK, Rust Android targets, and cargo-ndk. Desktop builds need the platform libraries listed in Building. Cargo commands use Cargo; the optional native Bazel backend is described there too. Run Cargo with at most four jobs.

License

MIT. See LICENSE; third-party licenses are in NOTICE and in the app under Settings, About, Licenses.
